title: Some Roman concrete has lasted 2,000 years, and may even self-heal
body: Roman harbour walls and buildings like the Pantheon have stood for around two millennia. Their concrete mixed lime with volcanic ash, and in seawater this slowly grows rare minerals such as aluminous tobermorite that strengthen it. A 2023 study also suggested that small lumps of lime left in the mix can dissolve into cracks and reseal them. Modern concrete is stronger, but steel-reinforced marine structures can decay within decades.
